# CONTENT.md — the book of the game

*Generated by `tools/systems.mjs` on 2026-10-07 from the shipped module. Every count below is read
out of the tables the game actually runs on — if a table changes, regenerate and this file changes with it.*

**The short version:** one run is 168 quarters (age 23 → 65). There are 87 scripted events plus 26 multi-stage arcs, 166 distinct actions behind 43 screens in 5 tabs and 24 sub-routes.

**The mental model.** At any moment a turn gives you five things to spend: **hours** (career and personal actions),
**money** (goods, assets, business capacity), **capital** (deals, contracts, land, franchises), **influence**
(the board, the group, the register) and **your household** (roles, perks, the people in your life). Every one of them
takes a quarter to pay off, and some of them schedule a bill you will not see for a year — which is the whole game.

---

## 1. What happens every quarter (the engine room)

Advancing a quarter runs these steps, in this order. Confirmed present in the module at generation time:

| # | step | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `flushPending` | consequences that were scheduled in earlier quarters come due |
| 2 | `stepEra` | the era can turn: ordinary times, boom, crunch, devaluation |
| 3 | `stepMarket` | inflation, FX, asset prices move |
| 4 | `maybeSwan` | a rare shock: the swan deck |
| 5 | `stepAssets` | your holdings pay out or fall |
| 6 | `simBusiness` | the business trades: capacity, demand, price, staff, upkeep |
| 7 | `stepGovernance` | the board, covenants, resolutions and the register |
| 8 | `stepGroup` | group accounts, breaches and cross-default |
| 9 | `stepHouse` | the household: roles, perks, asks |
| 10 | `stepPersonal` | health, stress, happiness, family, reputation |
| 11 | `stepCast` | the people in your life move: news, illness, death, asks |
| 12 | `stepRival` | the rival does something you may have to answer |
| 13 | `refreshDeals` | new capital opportunities appear |
| 14 | `refreshContractOffers` | clients put work on the table |
| 15 | `resolveDeals` | deals you committed to land: win or lose |
| 16 | `maybeOfferPartner` | somebody asks for a stake in your business |
| 17 | `snapshot` | the quarter is recorded for the charts |
| 18 | `checkEnd` | insolvency, health, retirement, the season finish line |
| 19 | `dueThread` | a story you started comes back for its next stage |
| 20 | `pickEvent` | the event deck: 62% chance of something happening |
| 21 | `year review` | every fourth quarter: the annual review modal |

The quarter also resets your **hours** (the one resource that never carries over) and ages you one quarter.

## 2. How a run ends

| ending | condition |
|---|---|
| **retire** | You reach 65, or turn 168 (42 years). The run closes on its own terms. |
| **season** | The season finish line you joined, or set, arrives. It takes precedence over every other ending. |
| **bankrupt** | Cash is deeply negative, debts exceed ₦1m and credit is under 22. On Hardcore the run ends here; below it, assets are seized and you continue with less. |
| **health** | Health reaches zero. Nothing buys it back at that point. |

### Policy events — the country does something to everyone — 12

| event | what it is, and what it asks of you |
|---|---|
| **Fuel subsidy removed overnight** | Pump price triples before dawn. Transport, food and diesel repriced by lunchtime. |
| **Currency devalued at the official window** | The central bank unification lands. Importers reprice everything within a week. |
| **Cash redesign / naira scarcity** | New notes, no notes. POS operators become the most powerful people in the country for six weeks. |
| **Monetary policy committee hikes aggressively** | Borrowing gets expensive. Fixed income suddenly pays; equities and property stop moving. |
| **Central bank begins an easing cycle** | Credit loosens. Cheap money returns and risk assets breathe again. |
| **Oil price collapse** | The budget gaps widen, the currency wobbles, and government contracts stop paying. |
| **Foreign investment returns** | Capital floods in. Valuations, land prices and confidence move together. |
| **National grid collapses — again** | Eleven days of darkness. Diesel sellers and solar installers have a very good quarter. |
| **Power supply improves unexpectedly** | A new independent grid deal lands. Businesses quietly stop budgeting for diesel. |
| **New tax regime takes effect** | Withholding, VAT and levies get restructured. Compliance costs go up for everyone formal. |
| **Bank recapitalisation directive** | Lenders must raise capital. Credit to small business dries up for two quarters. |
| **Security incident spooks investors** | A high-profile incident dominates the news. Logistics routes lengthen, insurance rises. |

### Negotiation tactics (deals, salaries, rent) — 7

| tactic | what it does |
|---|---|
| Anchor hard | Name a number near your best case and defend it. Moves them a long way when it works. |
| Argue it with numbers | Comparables, margins, what the market actually pays. Effective and low-risk if your finance skill is real. |
| Make a genuine concession | Move meaningfully to unlock movement from them. Costs you, nearly always closes. |
| Hold firm and say nothing | Free. Works when they are under time pressure and badly when they are not. |
| Trade a term instead of price | Give something that costs you less than cash: notice period, payment days, exclusivity, a title. |
| Use your leverage | Remind them, concretely, what you bring and what it costs them to lose you. You can only spend this once. |
| Walk away | Ends it. Sometimes the only leverage you ever actually had. |

## 6. What it costs you when it goes wrong

| mechanism | where | what actually happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Delayed consequences** | `flushPending` | A decision can schedule its own bill: `{turn, title, text, eff}`. It arrives as a modal, on the quarter it comes due. |
| **Insolvency, below Hardcore** | `checkEnd` | Assets are seized against the debt, credit collapses to 14, stress +18, happiness −14, reputation −10. You continue with less. |
| **Debt service** | `stepPersonal / budget` | Interest and repayments are drawn every quarter; credit score gates what you can borrow next. |
| **Inflation** | `stepMarket` | Cash loses purchasing power every quarter. The currency can also devalue, which hurts imports and helps exporters. |
| **Covenants** | `COVENANT_KINDS` | Leverage, cover, distributions, capex, liquidity and owner drawings. Breach is recorded and priced. |
| **Group cross-default** | `stepGroup` | A breach in one group company can pull the others in. |
| **Board** | `stepGovernance` | Directors have tempers and patience; resolutions pass or fail on votes, and the register records both. |
| **Rival** | `stepRival` | A competitor undercuts, poaches or expands; ignoring it has a cost. |
| **Cast** | `stepCast` | Friends, siblings, parents and partners age, ask for money, get ill and die. |
| **Stress and health** | `stepPersonal` | High stress erodes health and happiness; low happiness bleeds into output. |
| **Business failure** | `simBusiness` | Without capacity, staff, price or demand, revenue falls and upkeep still lands. |
| **Deals** | `resolveDeals` | Committed capital is at risk: the deal wins or loses, on the odds you were shown. |
| **Partner offers** | `maybeOfferPartner` | Above ₦3m revenue, somebody asks for a stake. Accepting changes who owns the business. |
| **Arcs** | `dueThread / maybeStartArc` | Stories have stages; a stage not answered comes back on its own schedule. |
